lastText: File ClosedThe Wing That Formed Too LateMinor DefeatThe War Cabinet and Chiefs of Staff, 1939–1945End of hostilities: JUNE 1945 (PROJECTED)Immediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives close to the historical schedule, around June 1945. The campaign's human cost lands close to the historical one on the Western front: lighter, by a wide margin, than the war the Soviet Union fought over the same years. Market Garden's reach for Arnhem was scaled back before it happened rather than mourned after: Browning's private reservation taken seriously instead of overruled. The Scheldt was cleared before the autumn's offensives rather than after: Antwerp opened weeks early, and the priority error most postwar assessments rank among the campaign's costliest was simply not made. The Mediterranean Fleet was sent against the German convoys off Crete, as it was, and paid three cruisers and six destroyers for an island that was lost anyway. Germany's defeat was never a variable Western Allied command decisions controlled, only its timing, its cost, and the shape of the peace that followed it.One Year LaterA year past victory in Europe, the machinery of occupation is running on the arrangements this campaign's own conferences (Tehran, Yalta, the ones this command actually attended) settled or failed to settle in advance.
